questions.cardText:
[Chemistry] What gives onions their distinctive smell?
A. Capsaicin
B. Sulfur compounds
C. Citric acid
Answer: B. The distinctive smell of onions is primarily due to sulfur compounds. When onions are chopped or crushed, these compounds are released, creating their characteristic pungent aroma.
questions.de: Welche Art von chemischen Verbindungen gibt Zwiebeln ihren typischen Geruch, der beim Schneiden freigesetzt wird?
questions.en: What kind of chemical compounds gives onions their distinctive smell, released when they are chopped?

timeline.labelEn: Linnaeus names the genus Allium, the onions and garlic, whose sulfur compounds give their smell
timeline.labelDe: Linné benennt die Gattung Allium (Zwiebeln, Knoblauch), deren Schwefelverbindungen ihren Geruch ausmachen

questions.notes: More precisely organosulfur compounds derived from cysteine (Allium plants grown without sulfur lose their smell).

questions.cardText:
[Art History] What is the “impressionism” art movement known for?
A. Religious and mythological themes
B. Not having clear subjects
C. Capturing outdoor light’s changing qualities
Answer: C. This movement was named after Claude Monet’s painting “Impression, Sunrise.” Critics meant the term derisively, but the artists embraced it.
questions.de: Was wollten die Impressionisten, deren Bewegung nach Claude Monets Gemälde „Impression, Sonnenaufgang“ benannt ist, vor allem einfangen, oft beim Malen im Freien?
questions.en: What did the Impressionists, whose movement is named after Claude Monet's painting “Impression, Sunrise”, above all seek to capture, often painting outdoors?
questions.answerDe: Das Licht in seinen wechselnden Qualitäten

timeline.labelEn: The first Impressionist exhibition opens in Paris, showing Monet's 'Impression, Sunrise'
timeline.labelDe: Die erste Impressionisten-Ausstellung in Paris wird eröffnet, mit Monets „Impression, Sonnenaufgang“
